title: Squid Hunt in the Dark Using Flashing Light Signals
subject: Humboldt squid

scenes.text: Hundreds of squid hunt together in total darkness, and they never collide.
Humboldt squid hunt in packs at depths of 266 to 848 meters, where almost no sunlight reaches.
Their skin flashes and flickers. Researchers have counted 28 colour and flashing patterns.
Hundreds of tiny lights inside the body light up the skin like a screen from behind.
Scientists think the squid are signalling each other, and that is why a frenzied feeding shoal does not turn into a brawl.
They may be talking in light. In the dark, that is the only language that works.

description:
Hundreds of squid hunt together in total darkness, and they never collide.
Humboldt squid flash 28 colour patterns on their skin, lit from inside by tiny lights.
What would you say in a language of light?
first_comment: If you could only talk in colours, what would your first signal be?
